Manage and administer the mWater platform for all WASH projects.

Maintain user access and permissions within mWater.
Ensure timely updating of OMS, OCMS, Digital ITT, and WASH asset databases.

title: IT Officer
description:
Job Summary
1. Position Overview
The IT Officer is responsible for managing, maintaining, and securing the organization’s network infrastructure, access control hardware, and physical security systems. This role ensures maximum network availability, maintains reliable operational hardware (including CCTV and biometric systems), and delivers timely technical support to internal teams.

Network & Infrastructure Management
Device Configuration: Install, configure, and maintain enterprise network switches, routers, firewalls, and wireless access points (APs).
Network Topology & Traffic: Manage VLANs, subnets, routing protocols, and IP address allocation schemes (DHCP, DNS, Static IPs).
Performance & Uptime: Monitor network bandwidth, latency, and system performance; proactively diagnose and resolve network outages.
Cabling & Hardware Maintenance: Oversee structured cabling, patch panel mapping, server room rack cleanliness, and Power over Ethernet (PoE) deployment.
CCTV & Surveillance Systems
System Deployment: Install, configure, and maintain IP and analog CCTV cameras, NVRs/DVRs, and storage arrays (NAS/SAN).
Operations & Compliance: Manage continuous recording schedules, data archiving, camera positioning, and regular footage retrieval for audits or security reviews.
Data Integrity: Ensure compliance with organizational data retention policies and privacy regulations regarding footage access.
Biometric & Access Control Systems
Hardware Operations: Set up, calibrate, and maintain biometric attendance terminals and electronic door access controllers.
User Management: Enroll employee fingerprints, facial recognition profiles, and access cards; coordinate user role access rights.
System Integration: Troubleshoot hardware connectivity errors, sync discrepancies, and integration bridges with HR/payroll management software.
System Maintenance, Security & User Support
Updates & Backups: Execute routine firmware updates, security patching, and configuration backups across all routers, switches, NVRs, and controllers.
Documentation: Maintain accurate hardware asset inventories, network diagrams, configuration documentation, and logs.
Technical Support: Serve as Level 1 and Level 2 support for network connectivity, access control issues, and workstation hardware/software issues.

TCP/IP, VLANs, Subnetting, Routing protocols, Switches, Routers, Firewalls, Wi-Fi Controller Management, PoE
Surveillance Hardware
IP/Analog CCTV, NVR/DVR management, PoE Switch allocation, Video storage arrays
Access Control
Biometric terminals (Fingerprint/Facial Recognition), Magnetic locks, Door controllers, HR system integration

Network Availability: Achieve and maintain 99.5%+ uptime for core network infrastructure.
Incident Resolution Time: Resolve physical security hardware issues (CCTV/Biometric) within agreed SLA windows.

Advise the Board of Management on technology-related matters and emerging risks.

Evaluate the adequacy of management oversight over IT operations.

Evaluate the Bank's readiness to address technology disruptions and cyber threats.

Evaluate the Bank's ability to maintain critical services during disruptions.
Provide recommendations for strengthening operational resilience.

Technology risks and mitigation measures.
IT operational performance.
Regulatory compliance status.
Significant technology incidents.
Progress of major IT projects.

Core banking systems.
Information security programs.
Technology investments.
Outsourcing and vendor management.
Emerging technologies and innovation.
Support management and the Board in making informed technology decisions.

Log and maintain records of site failures, power issues, and network downtime for SLA tracking and reconciliation.
Monitor network performance tools (Red EMCO) for microwave and InfiNet devices, including ping latency and interference analysis, and support corrective actions to ensure timely issue resolution.
Monitor Air Control Alerting systems for network devices including device online/offline status, pole movement alerts, interference issues, hotspot connectivity failures, CCQ degradation, and bitrate issues, and take corrective or escalated action as required.
Maintain overall health monitoring of network devices in accordance with standard points.
Provide second-line and limited third-line technical support for customer and network-related issues.
Troubleshoot and resolve issues related to BTS sites, PTP links, wireless sectors, switches, routers, and other network infrastructure.
Perform troubleshooting and configuration support for network switches, including implementation of advanced features when required.
Resolve customer-side issues related to CPE (Customer Premises Equipment) and LAN networks using remote access tools.
Support firmware and IOS/software upgrades for wireless and network devices based on vendor updates and operational requirements.
Identify, analyze, and resolve customer connectivity issues remotely using diagnostic and remote support tools.
Generate and share weekly reports of inactive/non-usage customers with Sales, CRM, and Collections teams for further action.
Escalate bandwidth and capacity-related issues to CRM and Sales teams for review and adjustment of customer packages.
Maintain accurate records of customer installations in the designated database, including customer name, connected base station details, router model, bandwidth allocation (day/night), contact details (POC), and technical configuration information.
Record and manage demo customers’ complaints and ensure follow-up until resolution in the designated system.
Maintain hotspot user records in centralized databases, including credentials, package details, validity, and access point information.
Update internal communication groups (e.g., WhatsApp groups) for new installations, link termination, and network incident notifications, and inform customers of urgent technical issues when required.
Coordinate and arrange field teams for on-site visits when remote troubleshooting is not sufficient.
Maintain complete documentation of system monitoring events, incidents, and customer complaints in designated databases.
Respond to all customer inquiries, calls, emails, and complaints in a professional and timely manner.
Communicate planned and unplanned maintenance activities, outages, and service issues to customers via email, phone, or messaging platforms, ensuring confirmation and status updates.
Schedule and communicate maintenance activities for base stations, ensuring customers are notified at least 48 hours in advance.
Prepare shift-wise reports detailing completed tasks, ongoing incidents, and pending issues.
Ensure proper handover of all active tickets, incidents, and operational tasks to the next shift for continuity of service.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science (BCS).
Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in IT/network operations, preferably in ISP or telecom environments.
Strong communication skills with ability to interact effectively with customers and internal teams.
Fluency in Dari, Pashto, and English (spoken and written).
Working knowledge of Linux operating systems and programming/scripting fundamentals.

This role operates in a 24/7 shift-based NOC environment at UA Telecom. With full accountability for continuous system monitoring and customer service operations. The position requires rotational shifts, including nights, weekends, and public holidays, and demands high responsiveness in a fast-paced, time-critical environment.

Certifications such as Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA), Cisco Certified Network Associate – Wireless (CCNA Wireless), Cisco Certified Network Professional (CCNP), and Microsoft Certified IT Professional (MCITP) are highly advantageous for this role.
